days.heading: Arrive Athens, Plaka evening

facts.label: Transfer
facts.valueHtml: ATH airport -> Plaka ~40 min by taxi/metro

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Check in, wander Plaka & Anafiotika, early dinner

days.note: Land in Athens, drop bags near Plaka, and let the first evening be gentle: the pedestrian lanes of Plaka and the whitewashed island-in-the-city pocket of Anafiotika are the perfect jet-lag stroll before the islands begin.

spots.name: Plaka & Anafiotika
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · plakaIG · anafiotikaIG · athensFlickr

images.alt: Leafy taverna-lined lane climbing through Athens' Plaka quarter
Monastiraki square below the Acropolis, crowds and neoclassical facades
The Acropolis glowing at golden hour above the pine-covered Philopappou hill

spots.cost: Free to wander. Plaka is the old pedestrian quarter under the Acropolis — neoclassical lanes, tavernas, and souvenir stalls — and tucked into its upper slope is Anafiotika, a pocket of whitewashed, blue-doored Cycladic houses built by island masons in the 1840s. It is the trip’s gentle first taste of the islands, and a perfect jet-lag evening stroll.
spots.climate: Shaded, walkable, warm-evening. The narrow lanes hold shade even midday, and June evenings stay pleasant into the night. Anafiotika is residential — steep little stair-paths, worth the quiet respect (people live there).
spots.saveHtml: Save Make Plaka your free arrival-evening walk: climb the Anafiotika stairs for the rooftop-to-Lycabettus view at golden hour and eat where the locals do, off the main tourist strip.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A sit-down dinner on a vine-shaded Plaka terrace, plus a loukoumades (honey-doughnut) stop the kids will remember longer than any ruin.
spots.restoHtml:
• Plaka tavernas off the main lane — gyros, souvlaki, chips, and bread; the easiest picky-kid dinner in Athens
  • A Monastiraki pita counter — €3–4 pork/chicken gyros for a fast, cheap arrival-night meal
  • Loukoumades shop — hot honey doughnuts for dessert as the jet-lag treat
spots.altboxHtml:
• Anafiotika at golden hour for the whitewashed-village preview and the best rooftop light.
  • National Garden for a shaded, free morning with the 8-year-old before the Acropolis.
  • Panathenaic (Kallimarmaro) Stadium for a quick run around the marble track.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Anafiotika neighborhood guideAthens in June — weather

days.travelNote: Travel day - arrive ATH, settle in Plaka.

days.heading: The Acropolis
days.feel: The Parthenon, then the Acropolis Museum

facts.label: Heat rule
facts.valueHtml: Go at 8am open or after 6pm - midday is brutal

days.note: The one big culture day: the Acropolis at opening or late afternoon to beat the June heat, with the air-conditioned Acropolis Museum as the kid-friendly companion. Book the timed-entry slot in advance. Repack tonight for tomorrow’s ferry.

spots.name: The Acropolis & the marble city
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · acropolisIG · parthenonIG · athensFlickr

images.alt: Parthenon marble columns rising against a deep blue sky
The full Acropolis citadel on its rock above the treeline of Athens
The Caryatid porch of the Erechtheion on the Acropolis

spots.cost: The headline is the Acropolis: a combined site ticket is about €30 adult in summer; children under 5 are free and non-EU kids 6–25 pay a reduced ~€15, so a family of four runs roughly €75–90 (~$85–100). Since 2024 entry is a mandatory timed slot — book online at hhticket.gr and arrive in your 15-minute window. The separate Acropolis Museum is ~€15 (summer) and is the air-conditioned, kid-friendly companion.
spots.climate: Hot, dry, sunny inland. June highs average ~30°C / 86°F and there is almost no shade on the rock. Go at opening (~8am) or after 6pm; the midday climb is brutal for an 8-year-old. Carry 2+ liters of water, hats, and sunscreen; sunset is ~9pm, so a late-afternoon visit stays comfortable.
spots.saveHtml: Save Book the earliest timed slot to beat the heat and the cruise crowds, and skip the paid guided tours — the free hilltop climb to Areopagus or Filopappou gives the postcard Parthenon view for nothing.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pair the site with the Acropolis Museum (the AC and the scale models are a genuine kid win), then a rooftop dinner in Plaka or Monastiraki with the lit Parthenon overhead.
spots.restoHtml:
• Tzitzikas kai Mermigas (Syntagma) — big Greek menu, famous fresh chips and grilled-pork pita the kids reliably eat
  • A Plaka pizza/pasta trattoria — wood-fired pizza and simple pasta a two-minute walk from the site for the pickiest eater
  • A family taverna at the foot of the Acropolis — pork or chicken gyros, tzatziki, bread, and fries as the dependable fallback
spots.altboxHtml:
• Late-afternoon Acropolis instead of morning if you want the marble in warm light and cooler air.
  • Acropolis Museum first on a scorching day for the AC, then the rock at 6pm.
  • Cape Sounion (Temple of Poseidon) as a half-day sea-cliff sunset drive if you have a spare afternoon.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Acropolis timed tickets — hhticket.grAcropolis Museum — plan your visit

days.heading: Ferry to Naxos, Portara sunset

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Sunset through the marble Portara your first evening

days.note: Morning high-speed ferry from Piraeus out to Naxos, the greenest and most kid-friendly Cyclade. Collect the rental car, settle into Chora, and walk out to the Portara for sunset — the great marble doorway framing the sun over the Aegean.

spots.name: Naxos Chora & the Portara at sunset
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · portaraIG · naxosIG · naxoschoraFlickr

images.alt: Sun bursting through the marble Portara gateway on Naxos at sunset
The Portara standing on its islet linked to Naxos Chora by a causeway
Naxos Chora and its harbour lit up at dusk seen from the water

spots.cost: Free, 24/7. The Portara — the colossal marble doorway of an unfinished 6th-century-BC Temple of Apollo — stands on the islet off Naxos Town, a 10-minute walk across the causeway and up ~75 steps. It frames the sunset like nothing else in the Cyclades. Below it, Naxos Chora tumbles up to a Venetian kastro of stone lanes.
spots.climate: Warm, sunny, breezy. June air tops out around ~28°C / 82°F with low humidity, and the sea has warmed to ~22°C / 72°F. Afternoons can pick up a north breeze (the meltemi is mild in early/mid June); the causeway to the Portara is exposed and glorious at golden hour.
spots.saveHtml: Save The Portara is free — make it your first-evening ritual, arriving 45 minutes before sunset for a spot on the marble. Wander the kastro lanes for nothing rather than paying for a walking tour.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A waterfront-taverna dinner in Chora after the sunset, then a Naxos kitron (citron) liqueur nightcap for the grown-ups.
spots.restoHtml:
• Caya (Naxos Town) — Italian-Mediterranean with wood-fired pizza and gnocchi, an easy picky-kid win
  • Scirocco (Protodikeiou Sq.) — family-run since 1995, modern Greek with pasta and grilled plates
  • Trata (Agios Georgios beach) — classic beach taverna: grilled meat, fries, pasta, calamari
spots.altboxHtml:
• Portara at dawn if you want it crowd-free instead of the sunset scrum.
  • Kastro walk + Della Rocca-Barozzi tower for a bit of Venetian history in the lanes.
  • Naxos Town harbor stroll for a low-key first evening if the flight day was long.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Portara — visiting infoNaxos in June — climate

days.travelNote: Travel day - Piraeus to Naxos by ferry.

days.heading: Naxos beach day

facts.label: Water
facts.valueHtml: Sea ~22°C / 72°F - the warmest, easiest swim of the trip

days.note: The reason Naxos is the base: long crescents of golden sand and gentle shallow water at Agios Prokopios and Plaka — the best family swimming on the trip. Swim in the calm morning, and keep the south beaches in your pocket if the afternoon breeze picks up.

spots.name: Agios Prokopios & Plaka: the long sandy beaches
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · agiosprokopiosIG · plakabeachIG · naxosFlickr

images.alt: The long sweep of sand at Plaka beach on Naxos meeting a calm sea
A turquoise Naxos bay backed by a whitewashed village and headland
A sheltered sandy cove with clear turquoise shallows on Naxos

spots.cost: The reason Naxos is the family base. Agios Prokopios is a Blue-Flag, 1.5 km crescent of golden sand with a gentle shallow shelf — the most kid-friendly swim on the trip. Sunbed-and-umbrella pairs run ~€20/day at the organized south end; the north end is free. Plaka beach next door is a 4 km ribbon of white sand and dunes. Water is a warming ~22°C / 72°F.
spots.climate: Sandy, shallow, west-facing. Warm sun and calm mornings; the meltemi, when it blows, hits these west-coast beaches strongest in the afternoon, so swim early and picnic late. For a truly wind-sheltered day, the south/east beaches (Agiassos, Kalantos) stay calmer.
spots.saveHtml: Save Park at the free north end of Agios Prokopios, bring your own umbrella, and swim before the afternoon breeze; a local bus (~€3.50) reaches the beaches if you skip the car that day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A front-row sunbed set with a beach-bar lunch, or a lesson at a Plaka/Mikri Vigla watersports center for the 13-year-old (windsurf/SUP).
spots.restoHtml:
• Beach-bar tavernas at Agios Prokopios — toasties, fries, pasta, and grilled fish steps from the sand
  • Caya or a Chora pizzeria — back in town for a reliable wood-fired-pizza dinner
  • Naxos Town gyros counters — cheap, fast picky-kid lunches between swims
spots.altboxHtml:
• Plaka beach dunes for a wilder, quieter stretch than Agios Prokopios.
  • Mikri Vigla for the windier watersports end if the teen wants a lesson.
  • Agiassos or Kalantos (south) as the meltemi-sheltered backup on a windy day.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Agios Prokopios guideNaxos June sea temperature

days.heading: Naxos mountain villages
days.daycost: Est. $130 · car day, tastings, taverna lunch

facts.label: Why
facts.valueHtml: Cooler, greener inland - a break from beach heat

days.note: Naxos is the one Cyclade with a real mountainous interior. Drive up through the Tragea olive valleys to Halki for a free citron-liqueur tasting, then marble-paved Apeiranthos — a cooler, greener half-day and a genuine change of pace from the sand.

spots.name: Halki & Apeiranthos: the mountain villages
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · apeiranthosIG · halkiIG · naxosFlickr

images.alt: A stone mountain village on Naxos looking out over the Aegean
A whitewashed Naxos hill village stepping down toward the sea
A bougainvillea-shaded taverna courtyard in a Naxos village

spots.cost: Naxos is the greenest, most mountainous Cyclade, and its inland villages are the antidote to a pure beach trip. Halki (~25 min up) is the old kitron capital: the free Vallindras distillery pours a family-friendly citron-liqueur tasting with a small museum. Apeiranthos (~30–40 min) is a marble-paved mountain village of Venetian towers and little museums. Both are free to wander; you just need the rental car and a couple of euros for coffee.
spots.climate: Cooler and greener up high. The drive climbs through Tragea olive valleys to villages several degrees cooler than the coast — a smart midday escape from beach heat or an afternoon meltemi. Marble lanes are shaded; bring grippy shoes for the cobbles.
spots.saveHtml: Save The villages cost nothing to explore and the Vallindras kitron tasting is free — make it a self-drive loop (Halki → Filoti → Apeiranthos) with a taverna lunch, no tour needed.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Lunch at a mountain taverna in Apeiranthos or Filoti with a view over the Tragea, plus a stop at the Fish & Olive ceramics gallery in Halki.
spots.restoHtml:
• Apeiranthos / Filoti mountain tavernas — grilled meat, fries, and local cheese with a valley view
  • Halki cafes on the square — toasties, sweets, and drinks around the kitron distillery
  • A bakery in Chalki or Filoti — cheese pies and pastries for a picky-kid car lunch
spots.altboxHtml:
• Temple of Demeter (Sangri) as an easy ancient-site add-on on the way up.
  • Melanes / Flerio kouros to hunt the giant unfinished marble statue lying in an orchard.
  • Mount Zas cave for a short hike with the teen if you want a leg-stretch.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Halki (kitron village) guideNaxos villages one-day drive

days.heading: Naxos flex + Portara

facts.label: Flex
facts.valueHtml: Wind-led: sheltered beach, Chora kastro, or watersports

days.note: A flex day — read the wind and choose: another shallow-beach morning, the Venetian kastro lanes of Chora, or a watersports lesson at breezy Mikri Vigla for the teen. A relaxed last Naxos evening before the island-hop resumes. Repack tonight.

days.heading: Ferry to Paros, Naoussa

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Naoussa fishing harbor at golden hour

days.note: The easiest transfer of the trip: a 30–40 minute ferry hop to Paros. Base in or near Naoussa, the Cyclades’ loveliest fishing village — a working harbor, a half-sunk Venetian fort, and lanes that glow at sunset.

spots.name: Naoussa: the fishing harbor at golden hour
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · naoussaIG · parosIG · naoussaparosFlickr

images.alt: A traditional wooden boat in Naoussa harbour on Paros at sunset
The pier and white village of Naoussa reaching into a turquoise bay
Fishing boats moored along the breakwater rocks at Naoussa

spots.cost: Free to soak up. Naoussa is the prettiest fishing village in the Cyclades: a working harbor of caiques and octopus drying on the quay, a half-sunk 15th-century Venetian kastro you can wade to, and a warren of white lanes that fill with tavernas at night. Golden hour (~18:30–19:30 in June) lights the boats and the fort — the trip’s most romantic evening, and it costs nothing but dinner.
spots.climate: Warm, bright, breezy. June air ~28°C / 82°F, sea ~22°C / 72°F. Paros is a windsurf island for a reason — the afternoon meltemi is real here — but Naoussa’s harbor and lanes are sheltered and calm at dusk.
spots.saveHtml: Save Wander the harbor and kastro for free, wade out to the ruined fort, and eat gyros on the quay rather than a full sit-down if the budget is tight.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A seafood dinner on the Naoussa waterfront at sunset, then a gelato walk through the lantern-lit back lanes.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pita Frank (Naoussa) — legendary ~€3.50 gyros, customizable, an instant kid favorite
  • Taverna Glafkos (Naoussa) — family-run, pasta and traditional plates on the water
  • Cuore Rosso (Parikia) — widely rated the island’s best pizza for the pickiest eater
spots.altboxHtml:
• Parikia old town + Panagia Ekatontapyliani (the 4th-century "church of 100 doors") for a quieter afternoon.
  • Lefkes mountain village for a stone-lane, bougainvillea half-day inland.
  • Naoussa kastro swim off the rocks by the harbor fort.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Naoussa, Paros guideParos in June — weather

days.travelNote: Travel day - Naxos to Paros by ferry.

days.heading: Ferry to Milos, Plaka sunset

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Klima syrmata + Plaka castle at sunset

days.note: Ferry southwest to Milos, the volcanic showpiece. Collect the car, settle in Adamas or Pollonia, and ease in with the island’s villages: the color-doored syrmata of Klima and a sunset climb to the castle above whitewashed Plaka.

spots.name: Plaka, Klima & the fishing coves
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · klimaIG · plakamilosIG · firopotamosFlickr

images.alt: The colourful syrmata boathouses of Klima reflected in calm Milos water
Fishing boats and painted boathouses in the Mandrakia cove on Milos
A white chapel and Greek flag above the fishing coves of Milos

spots.cost: The island’s village-and-cove side. Klima is a row of syrmata — two-level fishermen’s houses with brightly painted doors carved right into the rock at the waterline, glowing at sunset. Hilltop Plaka is the whitewashed capital, with a free 200-step climb to a Venetian castle for one of the Aegean’s best sunsets. Firopotamos and Papafragas are tiny, photogenic swim coves. All free; you just need the car.
spots.climate: Warm evenings, west-facing sunsets. Klima and the Plaka castle both face west for the sunset; June nights are balmy for a village dinner. Papafragas has a steep, rocky final descent to the water — sturdy shoes, and mind the little ones.
spots.saveHtml: Save Klima, Plaka, and the castle are all free — make a sunset loop of them, park once and walk, and swim at Firopotamos rather than a paid beach.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Sunset dinner in Plaka after the castle climb, or a couple of nights based in pretty Pollonia at the quieter north end.
spots.restoHtml:
• Plaka / Trypiti tavernas — grilled plates and pasta with the sunset view
  • Adamas: Egoist & Gyros of Milos — burgers, pasta, and gyros for the picky crew
  • Pollonia seafront — relaxed pizza-and-seafood dinners at the north end
spots.altboxHtml:
• Plaka castle at sunset for the island’s cinematic view (200 steps up).
  • Mandrakia — another photogenic syrmata fishing hamlet if Klima is busy.
  • Firopotamos swim as the calm, sandy-ish north-coast cove.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Klima travel guideMilos best sunset spots

days.travelNote: Travel day - Paros to Milos by ferry.

days.heading: Kleftiko boat day

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Full-day Kleftiko cruise (book early in the stay)

days.note: The marquee: a full-day boat to Kleftiko’s white sea caves and arches, with swim and snorkel stops along the roadless southwest coast. Keep it flexible — if the wind is up, this is the day that slides into the buffer.

spots.name: Kleftiko: the sea caves by boat
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · kleftikoIG · milosIG · kleftikomilosFlickr

images.alt: Aerial of Kleftiko's white sea stacks and yachts in turquoise water
A towering white sea arch rising from the water at Kleftiko
A small boat gliding into a white sea cave arch at Kleftiko

spots.cost: The trip’s marquee: Kleftiko — a cathedral of white volcanic sea caves, arches, and stacks on Milos’s roadless southwest coast — is reachable only by boat. A full-day group cruise from Adamas or Pollonia runs ~€120–175/person (kids often reduced) and typically includes several swim/snorkel stops, gear, and lunch on board; a family of four is roughly €400–620 (~$450–680). Operators include Horizon, Excellent Yachting, Polco Sailing, and Zephyros.
spots.climate: The wind-dependent day — the one to keep flexible. Kleftiko faces the open southwest, so a strong meltemi can force operators to cancel or reroute at short notice. June is the calm shoulder (the meltemi peaks in July–August), and cancellations are uncommon, but this is exactly why the plan carries buffer days: book it early in the Milos stay so a blown-out day can slide.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take a larger group boat rather than a private charter, book directly with a Milos operator, and pick a morning departure when the sea is calmest.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A small-group or semi-private sailing catamaran to Kleftiko with fewer people, more swim time, and a proper on-board lunch.
spots.restoHtml:
• Lunch is aboard — most full-day Kleftiko cruises feed you on the boat, so this is a packed day
  • Adamas waterfront on return — Aktaion for pizza/pasta or a gyros counter for the kids
  • Pollonia tavernas — if you sail from the north end, an easy seafood-or-pasta dinner after
spots.altboxHtml:
• Half-day Kleftiko motorboat tour if a full 9-hour day is too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Reschedule within the Milos stay if the wind is up — the built-in reason for three nights.
  • Papafragas + Sarakiniko by car as the no-boat backup if Kleftiko blows out entirely.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Kleftiko boat tours (GetYourGuide)Kleftiko by Horizon Yachts

days.heading: Sarakiniko + coves

facts.label: Light rule
facts.valueHtml: Sarakiniko at sunrise or ~6pm - no shade midday

days.note: The photo payoff: Sarakiniko’s blinding-white volcanic moonscape and its turquoise slot, best at sunrise or golden hour, plus the little swim-coves of Firopotamos and sea-carved Papafragas. A last, otherworldly Aegean day before the flight home. Repack tonight.

spots.name: Sarakiniko: the white moonscape
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · sarakinikoIG · milosIG · sarakinikobeachFlickr

images.alt: The narrow turquoise inlet cutting through Sarakiniko's white rock
Swimmers exploring the smooth white moonscape of Sarakiniko
The blinding white volcanic rock of Sarakiniko above a blue sea

spots.cost: Free, and unlike anywhere else on the trip. Sarakiniko is a moonscape of blinding-white, wind-smoothed volcanic rock rolling into a slot of turquoise water — the most photographed spot on Milos. There’s a small sandy patch and flat rock ledges to swim from, plus little caves to explore. Parking is free at the entrance; there is no shade and no facilities, so it’s a sunrise or late-afternoon place.
spots.climate: Bright, exposed, north-facing. The white rock throws light and heat, and Sarakiniko sits on the exposed north coast, so a strong meltemi makes the swim choppy — another calm-morning target. Go at first light for the empty moonscape or before sunset for the warm glow; midday is a glare-bomb with no shade.
spots.saveHtml: Save It’s free — come at sunrise or ~6pm for soft light and no crowds, bring your own water and shade, and swim off the ledges rather than paying for anything.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pair a sunset here with dinner in hilltop Plaka village nearby, or add a short boat/kayak to the adjacent sea caves.
spots.restoHtml:
• Adamas tavernas (~10 min) — Egoist for burgers/pasta, or Gyros of Milos for the kids
  • Pollonia (~10 min) — relaxed seafront pizza and pasta if you’re based north
  • Plaka village tavernas — combine with the sunset-castle climb above
spots.altboxHtml:
• Sunrise Sarakiniko for an empty moonscape and the best light.
  • Papafragas cove (nearby) for a sea-carved gorge swim — sturdy shoes for the steep descent.
  • Firopotamos for a calmer, sandier north-coast swim if Sarakiniko is windy.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Sarakiniko beach guideMilos June sea temperature

days.heading: Fly Milos -> Athens (buffer)
days.feel: Island air, safety night in Athens

facts.label: Why buffer
facts.valueHtml: Protects the international connection + meltemi delays

days.note: Fly the 40-minute domestic hop from little Milos (MLO) back to Athens and overnight near the airport. This buffer night is deliberate: it protects the next-day international connection and absorbs any meltemi-driven ferry or flight delay from the islands.
days.travelNote: Travel day - fly Milos to Athens, overnight buffer.
